en.title: X-Men '97: Marvel Promises Smoother Sailing for Season 3 After Production Woes
en.summary: The beloved animated revival is officially renewed for a third season, with producers vowing to avoid the lengthy production delays that plagued its earlier seasons. Fans can expect a more consistent release schedule going forward.
en.body:
After a two-year hiatus that tested the patience of even the most dedicated fans, **X-Men '97** is officially gearing up for its third season. Producers are making a clear commitment to fans, promising that the production pipeline will be significantly smoother than the one that led to the substantial gap between seasons one and two. This reassurance comes directly from the creative team, who learned valuable lessons from the challenges faced during the show's initial run.

Executive producer **Larry Houston**, a veteran of the original **X-Men: The Animated Series**, stated directly that the production issues experienced previously "won't occur again." He emphasized that the long wait was a "one-off," and that lessons learned will ensure seasons three and four arrive without similar delays. This sentiment is echoed by **Marvel animation head Brad Winderbaum**, who anticipates annual releases for both upcoming seasons, free from the earlier production mishaps. This proactive stance aims to rebuild confidence and ensure the continued momentum of this critically acclaimed revival.

## The Road to Season Three

The journey for **X-Men '97** has been anything but smooth behind the scenes. The series debuted in March 2024 to widespread critical acclaim and passionate fan reception, quickly becoming a must-watch for a new generation and nostalgic fans alike. However, its debut was shadowed by significant behind-the-scenes changes, including the departure of series creator **Beau DeMayo**. While Marvel executives are keen to move the narrative forward into a post-DeMayo era, the impact of these changes on the production timeline was undeniable. The long gap between seasons one and two, while attributed by producers to production challenges, has inevitably led fans to speculate about the underlying causes, especially given the timing of these events.

## What This Means for Fans

For the dedicated **X-Men '97** fanbase, this announcement is a beacon of hope. The promise of annual seasons means less agonizing waiting and more immediate access to the unfolding mutant saga. The series has masterfully captured the spirit of the original while introducing compelling new storylines and character arcs, making the prospect of consistent new content incredibly exciting. The stakes are high for Marvel Animation to deliver on this promise, ensuring that the show's narrative momentum isn't derailed by further production hiccups. The community is eager to see the **X-Men** continue their adventures without interruption, solidifying the revival's place as a flagship series for the platform.

## What's Next

Fans can anticipate **X-Men '97** season two arriving in summer 2026, with season three expected to follow annually thereafter. Marvel appears committed to a more streamlined production schedule, ensuring the **X-Men**'s return is a consistent event for years to come.

content_raw: It can be difficult, when analyzing the wide, varied, and very human world of pop culture, not to see subtext where there isn’t any. Take, for instance, recent comments made by producers on Disney+ animated series  X-Men ’97 , who’ve promised that the critically heralded cartoon won’t be repeating the two-year gap between its first and second seasons when its third one allegedly comes along next year. Executive producer Larry Houston—who worked on the original Fox animated series that the new show serves as a continuation of— told The Direct this week that, “Luckily, the production problems won’t occur again. There was a huge gap of time between [season] one and two. They’ve learned their lessons, so with [seasons] three and four, that won’t happen again… That was a one-off.” Marvel animation head Brad Winderbaum has made similar statements, expressing his belief that both a third and a fourth season of the series will arrive annually, free of any earlier production mishaps. All of which is pretty hard not to read in the context of the massive shake-ups that happened behind the scenes of the show, just as it was debuting back in March 2024—regardless of whether the firing of series creator Beau DeMayo amid allegations of sexual impropriety was connected to the gap. (DeMayo, who wrote or co-wrote all but three episodes of the show’s first season, had reportedly penned several scripts for the second by the time he was fired, although at least some of those were reportedly reworked.) Marvel execs, for their part, are pretty clearly trying to push the narrative around the show into a post-DeMayo phase. (Tricky, given how open he was about how personal some of the narratives in the first season, most especially its standout episode “Remember It,” were.) Although DeMayo remains an executive producer on the series, Winderbaum has given statements over the last year  emphasizing all the members of the creative team who have not been fired under a cloud of bitter recriminations and slightly off-putting OnlyFans posts: “Same director, same producers, same cast, many of the same writers, and it’s standing on the shoulders of giants.”  X-Men ’97  returns for its second season on July 1.
